title: Nigella Lawson
description: English food writer and TV cook (born 1960)
wiki_lead:
Nigella Lawson (born 6 January 1960) is an English food writer, television cook, and former journalist. Known for her relaxed and indulgent approach to cooking and food writing, she has sold more than 12 million cookery books worldwide to date, and has appeared on numerous television programmes in the United Kingdom and internationally. 
After graduating from the University of Oxford, Lawson began her career in journalism, working as a book reviewer and restaurant critic before becoming deputy literary editor of The Sunday Times in 1986. She left the staff position the following year to pursue freelance writing. In 1998, her first cookery book, How to Eat, was published and sold over 300,000 copies, becoming a best-seller. Lawsons's  second book, How to Be a Domestic Goddess, was published in 2000, winning the British Book Award for Author of the Year.
In the United Kingdom, Lawson hosted the cookery programmes Nigella Bites (1999–2001), Nigella Express (2007), Simply Nigella (2015), Nigella's Cook, Eat, Repeat (2020), and the ITV daytime chat show Nigella (2005). In the United States, she hosted the Food Network series Nigella Feasts (2006) and judged on the ABC cooking competition The Taste (2013–2014). She was a judge on the Australian cooking competition My Kitchen Rules (2022–2023). In 2026, Lawson became a judge on the Channel 4 baking competition The Great British Bake Off. 
In 2021, Lawson was nominated for a BAFTA. In June 2026, she was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature in recognition of her contribution to food writing. Her range of cookware, Living Kitchen, has a value of £7 million.

Early life
Nigella Lawson was born in 1960 in Wandsworth, London, one of the daughters of Nigel Lawson, Baron Lawson of Blaby (1932–2023), a business and finance journalist who later became a Conservative MP and Chancellor of the Exchequer in Margaret Thatcher's government, and his first wife, Vanessa Salmon (1936–1985), a socialite and the heiress to the J. Lyons and Co. fortune. Both her parents were from Jewish families. Her given name was originally suggested by her grandmother. Her family owned homes in Kensington and Chelsea.
Nigel and Vanessa Lawson divorced in 1980, when Nigella was 20. They both remarried: her father that year to a House of Commons researcher, Therese Maclear (to whom he was married until 2008), and her mother, in the early 1980s, to philosopher A. J. Ayer (they remained married until her mother's death). As her father was at the time a prominent political figure, Nigella found some of the judgements and preconceptions that were formed about her frustrating. She has attributed her unhappiness as a child, in part, to the problematic relationship she had with her mother.

grok_lead: Nigella Lucy Lawson (born 6 January 1960) is an English food writer, television presenter, and journalist celebrated for her cookery books and programmes that advocate indulgent, accessible home cooking rooted in personal pleasure rather than perfectionism. The daughter of Nigel Lawson, who served as Chancellor of the Exchequer under Margaret Thatcher, she graduated from the University of Oxford and initially pursued a career in publishing and restaurant criticism, rising to deputy literary editor of The Sunday Times by age 26. Lawson achieved widespread recognition with her debut cookbook How to Eat (1998), followed by bestsellers such as How to Be a Domestic Goddess (2000), Feast (2004), and Cook, Eat, Repeat (2020), which collectively emphasize sensory enjoyment, practicality, and the comforts of everyday feasting over dietary austerity. Her television career includes hosting series like Nigella Bites (1999â2001), Nigella Express (2007), and Nigella: At My Table (2017), and in January 2026 it was announced that she would replace Prue Leith as a judge on The Great British Bake Off. Her relaxed, narrative-driven style has drawn both praise for demystifying cooking and scrutiny for its hedonistic tone amid shifting cultural attitudes toward food and body image.
